page: Amazon Web Services r5d.8xlarge is a fifth-generation memory-optimized instance managed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system provides 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical Intel Xeon 8259CL cores running at a base clock speed of 3.1 GHz, utilizing two threads per core. Memory capacity totals 256 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, offering an 8 GB allocation per vCPU. Hardware features include an integrated 1200 GB NVMe SSD volume for high-speed local storage, a 10 Gbps baseline network interface, and CPU instruction support for AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and BMI2.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate solid multi-core computational throughput alongside average memory subsystem performance. Multi-threaded evaluations such as multi-core stress-ng reached 27516.04 and Geekbench multi-core achieved 9535.0, reflecting stable scaling across its 32 vCPUs. Memory testing yielded 110.87 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 49.04 GB/sec for large-block writes. Conversely, single-thread performance is relatively modest, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 1048.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1304.29. Similarly, large language model prompt processing on a 70B parameter model scored poorly at 3.89 tokens per second due to the absence of dedicated GPU hardware.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, bundling 1200 GB of high-performance local NVMe SSD storage directly with large DDR4 memory capacity eliminates the throughput latency overhead of separate networked volumes for temporary scratch space. While single-thread limitations make it less appropriate for execution paths bottlenecked on single-core speed, its 25.82 million Redis SET operations per second and 10646.23 Passmark database operations score demonstrate strong suitability for concurrent memory-intensive tasks. The r5d.8xlarge instance is effective for relational databases, in-memory caching systems, distributed data analytics, and batch ETL processing.
description: Amazon Web Services r5d.8xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is equipped with 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores from an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz, paired with 256 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz. The configuration integrates 1200 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a 10 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results indicate balanced multi-threaded performance, recording 27516.04 on multi-core stress-ng tests and 25.82 million operations per second on Redis SET workloads, while single-threaded tasks register lower relative scores. The inclusion of bundled high-speed ephemeral NVMe storage reduces reliance on external block devices for temporary scratch space. Given its memory-to-vCPU ratio and high-capacity storage, r5d.8xlarge is designed for distributed relational databases, in-memory caches, analytics engines, and high-throughput data ingestion workloads.
